newsitem.title: CANADA: BioChem Pharma falls in vigorous trading.
newsitem.headline: BioChem Pharma falls in vigorous trading.

text.p: Shares of BioChem Pharma Inc fell on Tuesday as the market appeared to react coolly to clinical trial results released last week on its lamivudine drug.

On Nasdaq where Montreal-based BioChem Pharma's stock is most traded, its shares were off 4.75 to 18 at midday on a volume of more than 3.8 million shares. On the Toronto Stock Exchange, BioChem Pharma shares were down 7.50 to 24.50 on a turnover of 17,250 shares.
Analysts said BioChem's share price decline could be related to clinical trial results released last week on lamivudine, a drug under development for the treatment of Hepatitis B.
BioChem Pharma licensed lamivudine to Glaxo Wellcome Plc in 1990 and would receive royalties if the drug is approved for commercial sale.
Although BioChem Pharma and Glaxo said the trial results were "extremely encouraging," some analysts expressed reservations about the effectiveness of the drug in treating chronic Hepatitis B.
"I think the data was solid, but it maybe was a little bit below expectations," said Sven Borho, of New York-based Mehta and Isaly.

BioChem Pharma shares have been fairly volatile in the days before and after the April 10 announcement of the trial results in London. They slipped from more than 30 on Nasdaq in mid-February to below 22 in early April.
